chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the time of Zuhr, and he said: one cubit from the sun’s decline; and the time of 'Asr is one cubit from the time of Zuhr, so that is four foot-lengths from the sun’s decline.

key_terms.أَقْدَامٍ: foot-lengths, a traditional measure used to express the shadow
key_terms.الظُّهْرِ: the Zuhr salat, the midday prayer
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: a cubit, a traditional unit used here to measure shadow length
key_terms.زَوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the middle of the sky
key_terms.وَقْتِ: the appointed time or beginning time of an act of worship

ai.seo_question: When do the times of Zuhr and 'Asr begin according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith states the beginning times for the salat of Zuhr and 'Asr in relation to the sun’s decline from the meridian. It expresses these times using traditional measures of shadow length, making it a jurisprudential report about prayer timing.
